title: Powers of an element with smooth free localization are strictly standard
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a ring map of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and $a\in A$ such that the localization $A_a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a stably free $A_a$-module, i.e. $\Omega_{A_a/R}\oplus A_a^{\oplus s}\cong A_a^{\oplus t}$ for some integers $s,t\ge0$ (for instance free of finite rank, $s=0$). Then there is an integer $e_0\ge1$ such that $a^e$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] for every $e\ge e_0$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard, line 719), part (e) [(2) => a^e strictly standard for e >= e_0], with (3) => (2) of part (a) for free Omega

proof.text: (The localized conormal sequence; $(I/I^2)_a$ is stably free.) Choose a presentation $A\cong P/I$, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $I=(g_1,\dots,g_t)$ finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Since $A_a$ is smooth over $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split] gives a split short exact sequence of $A_a$-modules $0\to(I/I^2)_a\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i\to\Omega_{A_a/R}\to0$, so $(I/I^2)_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\cong A_a^{\oplus n}$. With $\Omega_{A_a/R}\oplus A_a^{\oplus s}\cong A_a^{\oplus t}$ (hypothesis) we get $(I/I^2)_a\oplus A_a^{\oplus t}\cong(I/I^2)_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\oplus A_a^{\oplus s}\cong A_a^{\oplus n+s}$. Put $r=t$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard, line 719), part (e): 'Choose a presentation A = R[x_1..x_n]/I with I finitely generated. By assumption we have a short exact sequence ... which is split exact. Hence (I/I^2)_a (+) Omega is free ... (I/I^2)_a is stably free as well'

proof.text: (Adding $r$ variables makes the localized conormal module free.) Let $N=n+r$, $P'=P[x_{n+1},\dots,x_N]$, and $P'\to A$ the surjection extending $P\to A$ with $x_{n+k}\mapsto0$; its kernel is $J=IP'+K$, $K=(x_{n+1},\dots,x_N)$, generated by $g_1,\dots,g_t,x_{n+1},\dots,x_N$ (finitely generated). Claim: $\varphi:I/I^2\oplus A^{\oplus r}\to J/J^2$, $(g\bmod I^2,(b_k))\mapsto g+\sum_k\tilde b_kx_{n+k}\bmod J^2$ ($\tilde b_k\in P'$ lifts of $b_k$) is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. It is well defined since $I^2\subseteq J^2$ and changing $\tilde b_k$ by an element of $J$ changes the sum by an element of $JK\subseteq J^2$. Surjective: $P'=P+K$, so $IP'\subseteq I+IK\subseteq I+J^2$ and $P'x_{n+k}\subseteq Px_{n+k}+J^2$. Inverse: for $g\in J$ write $g=g_0+\sum_kx_{n+k}q_k$ with $g_0=g(x_1,\dots,x_n,0,\dots,0)\in P$; $g_0\in J\cap P=I$ (the kernel of $P\to P'/J=A$), and the classes $\bar q_k\in A$ do not depend on the choice of the $q_k$ (two choices differ by a syzygy of $x_{n+1},\dots,x_N$, whose entries lie in $K\subseteq J$). Set $\psi(g)=(g_0\bmod I^2,(\bar q_k))$. For $g,g'\in J$: $(gg')_0=g_0g'_0\in I^2$ and $gg'-(gg')_0=\sum_kx_{n+k}(gq'_k+g'_0q_k)$ with $gq'_k+g'_0q_k\in J$, so $\psi(J^2)=0$; $\psi$ is additive and $A$-linear, and $\psi\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}$. As $\varphi$ is surjective, it is an isomorphism. Localizing at $a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] and using step 1, $(J/J^2)_a\cong(I/I^2)_a\oplus A_a^{\oplus r}\cong A_a^{\oplus n+s}$ is a finite free $A_a$-module.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard, line 719), part (e): 'replacing the presentation chosen above by A = R[x_1..x_{n+r}]/J with J = (I, x_{n+1},..,x_{n+r}) for some r we get that (J/J^2)_a is (finite) free' (the isomorphism J/J^2 = I/I^2 (+) A^r is left to the reader there and written out here)

proof.text: (The presentation.) Choose a basis $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_c$ of the free $A_a$-module $(J/J^2)_a$, taking the empty basis ($c=0$) if $A_a=0$. Write $\beta_k=\bar g_k/a^{u_k}$ with $g_k\in J$; since $a$ is a unit of $A_a$, the classes $\bar f_k/1$ of $f_k:=g_k\in J$ form a basis too. Extend to generators $f_1,\dots,f_m$ of $J$ by adding the finitely many generators of step 2, so $m\ge c$ and $A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_N]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ is a presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Also $c\le N$: by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split] applied to $P'\to A$, $\mathrm d_a:(J/J^2)_a\cong A_a^{\oplus c}\to A_a^{\oplus N}$ has a left inverse; if $A_a\ne0$, reducing modulo a maximal ideal of $A_a$ gives an injective linear map $k^c\to k^N$ of vector spaces over a field $k$, so $c\le N$; if $A_a=0$ then $c=0$. Thus $0\le c\le\min(N,m)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard, line 719), part (e): 'Choose f_1,..,f_c in J which map to a basis of (J/J^2)_a. Extend this to a list of generators f_1,..,f_m in J. Consider the presentation A = R[x_1..x_{n+r}]/(f_1..f_m).' (the bound c <= n+r, needed by Definition 07C7, is added here)

proof.text: (Second condition of [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] for $a^e$, $e\ge e_1$.) Let $h\in P'$ be a lift of $a$. For $j=1,\dots,m-c$, in $(J/J^2)_a$ we have $\bar f_{c+j}/1=\sum_{k\le c}(\bar b_{jk}/a^{u})\bar f_k/1$ with $b_{jk}\in P'$, $u\ge0$; by the definition of equality in the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] there is $v\ge0$ with $a^{v}(a^{u}\bar f_{c+j}-\sum_k\bar b_{jk}\bar f_k)=0$ in $J/J^2$, i.e. $h^{u+v}f_{c+j}\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)+J^2$. Let $e_1$ be the maximum of the $u+v$ over $j$; for $e\ge e_1$, $h^ef_{c+j}=h^{e-e_1}h^{u+v}\cdot h^{e_1-u-v}f_{c+j}\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)+J^2$, as $(f_1,\dots,f_c)+J^2$ is an ideal and $J=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard, line 719), part (e): 'Then (equation-strictly-standard-two) holds for a^e for all sufficiently large e by construction.'

proof.text: (First condition for $a^e$, $e\ge ce_2$.) Let $D$ be the $N\times c$ matrix over $A$ with entries $D_{ij}=\overline{\partial f_j/\partial x_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]; it is the matrix of the composite $A^{\oplus c}\xrightarrow{(f_1,\dots,f_c)}J/J^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\bigoplus_{i=1}^NA\,\mathrm dx_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split] (for $P'\to A$), $\mathrm d_a$ has an $A_a$-linear left inverse $\lambda$; composed with the inverse of the basis isomorphism $A_a^{\oplus c}\cong(J/J^2)_a$ of step 3 it gives a $c\times N$ matrix $\Lambda$ over $A_a$ with $\Lambda D=1_c$ in $A_a$. Clearing denominators, $\Lambda=\Lambda_0/a^{u}$ with $\Lambda_0$ over $A$; then $\Lambda_0D-a^{u}1_c$ maps to $0$ in $A_a$, so $a^{v}(\Lambda_0D-a^{u}1_c)=0$ in $A$ for some $v$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. With $B=a^{v}\Lambda_0$ and $e_2=u+v$ we get $BD=a^{e_2}1_c$ over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors] (2) (applicable as $N\ge c$, step 3), $a^{ce_2}=\sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\},|I|=c}a_I\det(\overline{\partial f_j/\partial x_i})_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}$ for some $a_I\in A$ (a minor and its transpose have the same determinant). For $e\ge ce_2$, multiplying by $a^{e-ce_2}$ gives the same form for $a^e$ with coefficients $a^{e-ce_2}a_I$. (For $c=0$ the condition reads $a^e=a_\emptyset$ and holds trivially.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard, line 719), part (e): 'since (J/J^2)_a -> (+) A_a dx_i is a split injection we can find an A_a-linear left inverse. Writing this left inverse in terms of the basis f_1..f_c and clearing denominators we find psi_0 ... is multiplication by a^{e_0} ... By Lemma 07ET (lemma-parse-equation-strictly-standard-one, a special case of Algebra Lemma 07DQ, lemma-matrix-left-inverse) we see (equation-strictly-standard-one) holds for all a^{ce_0} and hence for a^e for all e >= ce_0'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Put $e_0=\max(1,e_1,ce_2)$. For $e\ge e_0$ the presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_N]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ and the integer $c$ with $0\le c\le\min(N,m)$ (step 3) satisfy both conditions of [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] for $a^e$ (steps 4 and 5, with the lift $h^e$ of $a^e$), so $a^e$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$.
